standard_prerequisites.name: Multiplication by the variable on the extended complex is injective with cokernel isomorphic to the original complex, so the associated total complex is quasi-isomorphic to the original complex
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the total complex as a resolution of the original complex, which justifies replacing the complex by it.

core_obligations: Choose a K-flat resolution of the given complex whose terms are flat modules, so that the derived tensor products can be computed from ordinary tensor products (proof lines 21228-21230).

Extend scalars to the polynomial algebra and observe that multiplication by the variable on each extended term is injective with cokernel the original term, so that the two-term double complex given by multiplication by the variable has an associated total complex quasi-isomorphic to the original complex (proof lines 21230-21240).

Record that this total complex is again K-flat over the polynomial algebra, so that the derived tensor product with the base can be computed as the ordinary tensor product with the base (proof lines 21242-21246).

Compute that tensor product in the displayed chain of equalities: the total complex reduces to the total complex of the zero map between two copies of the resolution, which is the direct sum of the resolution and its shift, giving the asserted isomorphism with the complex and its shift (proof lines 21247-21255).
proof_roadmap: Choose a K-flat resolution by flat modules (proof lines 21228-21230).
Build the double complex given by multiplication by the variable and note that its total complex is a K-flat resolution of the original complex (proof lines 21230-21246).
Tensoring with the base kills the variable, so the total complex becomes the direct sum of the resolution and its shift, which gives the isomorphism (proof lines 21247-21255).
difficulty_reason: The statement computes the derived tensor product of a complex along the projection from the polynomial algebra onto the base, obtaining the direct sum of the complex and its shift (statement lines 21217-21226). The proof chooses a K-flat resolution by flat modules, encodes the projection as the double complex given by multiplication by the variable, checks that its total complex is a K-flat resolution of the original complex because multiplication by the variable is injective with cokernel the original term, and then evaluates the tensor product with the base in a displayed chain of equalities which reduces to the direct sum of the resolution and its shift (proof lines 21228-21255). The replacement of the complex by the carefully chosen total complex is the device that makes the computation legitimate.
